Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining. Let me start with the outlook, and then I am going to take your questions. Next year will not be easy. Food inflation will stay high in the first half, and that is our main headwind. But we are not waiting for it to pass. From January, we are going to review prices every quarter, and we are going to protect the basic basket: the pass-through on those items will be two percent at most. Some of you asked about the new stores. We are opening eight in the first half, and the contracts are already signed. On guidance, nothing changes today. At the current run rate, we will have reached our volume target by October. If that changes, you will hear it from me first, not from the market.

One question comes up in almost every visa interview, and most people answer it badly. What are your plans after the course? The officer is not asking about your dreams. The officer is checking that you are going home. So answer with three futures. First, the arrangement that is already fixed: I am flying back the day after the course ends. Second, the plan: I am going to use the pricing models with my team at work. Third, a date, and what will be finished by then: by the end of the year, I will have presented the results to my board. Short, concrete, and nothing about staying. And one practical detail. Bring the return ticket. A date on paper says more than any promise.

First, she gives the outlook in one sentence. Then she names the main headwind. After that, she says what is already decided. Next, she gives the dates that are already fixed. Finally, she says what will be finished by a certain date.
